hook.line: AI designed a working engine part in two weeks, a job that takes engineers months.
hook.visual: Title 'THE FUTURE OF ENGINEERING' over a copper engine part on top, presenter at a mic below; top swaps to printed parts at 1.12 s, a fire test at 2.27 s.

beats.what: Split screen: copper engine part with title text on top, presenter below, first word at 0 s
Top clip swaps to printed parts; second visual change inside 1.2 s
Hot-fire test footage on top while the claim lands
Presenter disappears; full-width rounded-corner renders on a white page with short captions under them
Zoom punch into the turbine render as he says it is the first AI-designed engine part
Back to split screen, caption 'notice the shape' points the eye at the fractal geometry
Flame test clip again under 'human engineers rely on intuition' contrast
Cross-section render of the organic internal channels under 'generated by algorithms'
Return to presenter split for the closing line about machines designing
Last cut as he asks viewers to follow for more breakthroughs

why_it_works: Result first: the finished, working part and a live fire test are on screen before any explanation, so viewers stay to hear how
B-roll changes every ~1.5 s (median shot 1.53 s), so the eye always gets a new object while the voice stays steady
Strange, fractal shapes are their own pattern interrupt; the caption 'notice the shape' tells the viewer exactly where to look
Presenter returns at the start and end only, framing the footage as a trusted newsreader rather than carrying the visuals
weaknesses: Most text sits outside the safe zone (outside_safe_share 0.947), so captions risk being covered by TikTok UI
Caption position jumps between the split seam and the lower white area, so the eye has to re-find it after each layout change
Middle 40 s is pure narration over renders with no on-screen emphasis beyond captions
Generic 'follow for more' CTA gives no reason to comment or save
for_robert: Use the split layout's rhythm: Robert on the bottom half while the top half swaps a new visual every 1-2 s, and let Fred pop into the top half to 'present' the key object, then hand back to Robert full-frame for the close.
